result.title: A small cognitive core explains human behavior at scale
result.summary: Psychology has proposed many principles of cognition. Each, however, was developed in isolation, leaving their combined explanatory power unknown. We assembled a small set of established principles into one model, which we call COntextual Retrieval and Encoding (CORE). CORE consists of a hierarchy of episodic memories into which prediction errors are written and whose encoding, retrieval, and forgetting depend on context. Fitted jointly to 7,036,442 choices from 137 experiments, the model predicts human choices better than black-box models and reproduces 75% of reported behavioral effects when simulated. Moreover, its latent variables show classic signatures of Bayesian learning and event segmentation. Taken together, these findings suggest that a small cognitive core accounts for much of human behavior. They also open a path toward making psychology more than the sum of its parts, by building computational models on the entire experimental record.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文把若干既有认知原则整合为层级情景记忆模型 CORE，以预测误差写入、情境依赖的编码与检索，在 700 余万次人类选择上联合拟合，并报告其潜变量呈现贝叶斯学习与事件分割特征。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按预测误差写入、由情境门控读写」的层级记忆，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的更新与检索时机设计，以及用潜变量探针检验内部内容提供概念线索，尚需核查其与视觉推理任务的适配性。
